phase_0.boundary_condition: formal verification in Lean 4 against Mathlib with classical foundations (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound)

VINIT.justification: the void before any hypothesis is named — the empty space of an open question

TANCH.justification: the terminal anchor: every result in the domain is machine-checked in Lean, closing the system

AFWD.justification: forward morphism: exhibiting an explicit witness, formula, or construction (e.g., parametric family for Erdős-Straus, base-3 set for sumset)

AREV.justification: reverse morphism: reducing a case to a smaller one (multiplicative descent, contrapositive, induction step downward)

CLINK.justification: composition: chaining lemmas where the output of one feeds the hypothesis of the next (e.g., Kummer → Lucas → carry criterion → classification)

IMSCRIB.justification: self-reference: the classification's own fixed points (n = p^m for binomial gcd, n = a² for rep-tiling, the critical regime ⊙)

FSPLIT.justification: fork: parity (even/odd), congruence classes (mod 4, mod 12, mod 24), hypothesis types (D vs R), cycle length regimes (k=1,2,≥3)

FFUSE.justification: join: the boxed result that holds across all branches (e.g., h(n) = p or 1, f(2)=7, ratio vanishes for all n)

EVALT.justification: affirmative arm: the concrete object that proves existence (coloring, dissection, parametric solution, base-3 digits)

EVALF.justification: negative arm: the argument that no object can exist (no rep-6 similar dissection, no monotone tail, no tournament on 6 vertices)

ENGAGR.justification: paradice: the simultaneous holding of 'proven for almost all' and 'open for the rest' — the Erdős-Straus class n≡1 mod 4, 3∤n; the frontier values 193, 313, 457...; the gap between density and reciprocal hypotheses

IFIX.justification: ROM fixation: the permanent, append-only record of verification in the Mathlib library

phase_2.split_input: mathematical problem with multiple structural possibilities
split_outputs: constructive/explicit arm (parametric families, explicit constructions, closed forms)
non-constructive/descent arm (density arguments, impossibility, reduction to primes)
phase_2.fuse_result: a single classified result covering all cases — conflicting arms (explicit vs non-explicit) rejoin to B (both held), not to a single method
phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: the unformalized conjecture — no hypotheses, no structure, just the raw question
phase_3.true_description: a constructive witness has been exhibited and verified — the parametric family works, the dissection exists, the coloring is explicit
phase_3.false_description: an impossibility is proven — no such object can exist, the monotone tail fails, the tournament on 6 vertices cannot have S₂
phase_3.both_description: the paradice state: the theorem is proved for all cases by a case split, but the methods differ radically between branches (explicit formula vs density argument); or the problem is settled for almost all inputs yet the remaining frontier resists all known parametric methods while being known to have solutions

steps.domain_action: the domain opens with the unposed problems — alternating series monotonicity, binomial row gcd, odd cycle chords, Erdős-Fuchs average, Erdős-Straus, Kac interval, Landau's function, lcm growth, Lenz configuration, Mantel anti-Ramsey, monochromatic cycles, Ramsey ratios, rep-tiling, Roth-Behrend, Schütte numbers, SDR windows, sumset AP-free, syndetic duality
the terminal anchor is established — every result will be formalized in Lean 4 against Mathlib, depending on propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound

constructive hypothesis — for each problem, seek an explicit criterion or construction (rise criterion n·gₙ < pₙ, carry criterion for binomial coefficients, chord split a+b=ℓ, fibring identity for pair count, parametric families for 4/n)
primary case split — parity and congruence classes (n even/odd, n mod 4, n mod 12, n mod 24) and hypothesis types (density D vs reciprocal sum R)

T-arm — explicit witnesses: even n family (m, m+1, m(m+1)), n≡3 mod 4 family, n≡2 mod 4 family, n≡9 mod 12 family; base-3 construction for sumset; altitudes of equilateral for 6 congruent triangles; Paley tournament on 7 vertices
T-arm continues — forward morphisms building the constructions: clearing denominators, polynomial identities, rational parametrization of circle, quadratic form for Lenz distance
T-arm — chaining lemmas: Kummer → Lucas → digit criterion → prime power classification → exact gcd formula; ladder step → splitting criterion → three free families → exhaustion of monomial divisors
T-arm — self-reference at the fixed points: n = pᵐ for binomial gcd, n = a² for rep-tiling, the critical regime ⊙ where scale-free correlations appear

F-arm — impossibility proofs: no monotone tail (bounded gaps + superlinearity → rise), 6 not a rep-number (excluded from all three forms), no tournament on 6 vertices with S₂ (exhaustive search), no prime power in ω > log log interval (threshold at 16)

F-arm — descent arguments: multiplicative descent for Erdős-Straus (divisor represents multiple), contrapositive for chordless cycle (chord → shorter odd cycle), reduction of Ramsey ratio to base comparison
F-arm — chaining impossibilities: threshold log log 16 > 1 → monotone extension → prime power exclusion → interval length bounded by prime gaps

paradice engagement — the Erdős-Straus frontier (n≡1 mod 24, 624 values below 200k, 622 prime); the gap between density hypothesis (D) and reciprocal hypothesis (R) where primes live; the Schütte lower bound tight at f(2)=7 but open for k≥4; the SDR window where minₘ f(n,m)=n but f(n,n) diverges

rejoining at unified theorems — boxed results covering all branches: h(n) = p or 1; f(2)=7; ratio vanishes for all n; g(1..10) = 1,2,3,4,6,6,12,15,20,30; lcm > n log(n+1) from n=3; f₄(n) ≥ ⌊n²/4⌋; χ_S regimes 3, ⌊n/2⌋+3, Θ(n²/8); R(3,3)=6; g₃(n) values 1,3,8,22,60; D(2ⁿ)={0}
the verification loop — each theorem refers to its own Lean proof term, the fixed point of formalization

thirteenth fixation — Ramsey ratio bounds, base comparison, superexponential gap formalized

phase_5.compiler_frontend: Lean 4 kernel — translates mathematical intentions (definitions, theorems, proofs) into type-checked terms in dependent type theory
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Mathlib library — components communicate through shared definitions, typeclasses, and lemmas in the mathematical library; each paper imports and extends the common foundation
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Lean environment — state stored as declarations in the environment (defs, theorems, instances); retrieval via typeclass resolution and lemma application
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: proof development order — human-guided: problem statement → informal proof → formalization sketch → `have` statements → `sorry` elimination → compilation; the kernel evaluates in dependency order
phase_5.alfs_store: Mathlib4 (mathlib4/Mathlib) — the canonical bootstrap store; all results depend on propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound as the foundational axioms

phase_6.cycle_cost: human insight to find the exact criterion / classification / construction; CPU cycles for kernel checking
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: informal mathematical knowledge — conjectures, partial results, proof sketches
phase_6.post_cycle_state: formalized theorems in Mathlib — permanent, machine-verified, reusable as lemmas
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the cycle converts epistemic uncertainty (conjecture) into structural certainty (verified theorem) without loss; the information content is preserved and compressed into the library
